title: Nowym studentom
note:
C1 Block 2, unit 4 (C1-SPINE O2) — the Dative plural, and the block's sharpest homograph.

ZERO NEW FORMS, so teaches_lemmas is legitimately empty for the second time in this block (c1_adj_pl_loc was the first), on the copular_future / adj_inst / ze_clauses / passive / existential_tense convention. dobrym, nowym and malym have been TAUGHT since b2_adj_loc [136] and were re-used by b2_adj_inst [137]. The unit adds no string at all.

THE TRAP IS THE UNIT, and C1-SPINE named it in advance: "-ym is also the singular m/n Locative and Instrumental ending - same string, THIRD job. Name it." c1_adj_pl_loc's own note predicted the collision one node further back and told this unit to name it rather than assume it. What makes it worse than the block's earlier re-sightings is that the earlier ones changed CASE while holding NUMBER; this one changes NUMBER. w dobrym hotelu and z dobrym kolega are SINGULAR; dobrym studentom is PLURAL. Nothing in -ym says which. Slides 1 and 2 are that one fact, and the resolution given is the honest one: THE NOUN SETTLES IT. -om is the Dative plural and nothing else in the course ends that way, so the learner is told to read the noun, not the adjective.

THE PERSON-NOUN FORK CARRIES FORWARD FROM THE PREVIOUS NODE, and for the identical lexical reason. b2_dat_pl [154] taught exactly twelve Dative plurals and ELEVEN ARE PEOPLE (rodzicom, dzieciom, ludziom, studentom, kolegom, siostrom, corkom, synom, klientom, pacjentom, ciociom); the only non-person is kotom, and nauczycielom is verified NEW. This is the same twelve-noun shape as the Instrumental, so the same call was taken: person nouns carry the unit. It is safe on the same ground - THE DATIVE PLURAL HAS NO VIRILE SPLIT, -ym is uniform, and no virile form appears anywhere. No person noun takes an adjective in the NOMINATIVE; lekarka and dzieci appear as bare subjects only. C1-SPINE's standing fence ("virile forms appear nowhere before c1_adj_pl_virile") is intact.

duzy IS ABSENT AGAIN, and this time it is not even a choice this unit makes: b2_adj_dat [138] taught only dobremu, nowemu and malemu, exactly as b2_adj_gen dropped duzy and b2_adj_loc used dobry/nowy/maly/zimny. duzy has NO singular oblique anywhere in the course - duzym, duzego, duzej all verified NEW - so there is no singular Dative to contrast a plural against. The gap logged at c1_adj_pl_inst therefore stands unchanged and is now a block-wide fact rather than one unit's decision: duzy has duzych (Genitive and Locative plural) and nothing else oblique. c1_adj_pl_gym inherits it. The fix, if James wants the full four, is the gym or a later unit, not a forced sentence here.

THE SINGULAR-TO-PLURAL TABLE HAS ONLY TWO ROWS, and that is a lexical limit rather than an editorial one, stated so a reader does not think it was trimmed for space. A row needs a Dative singular AND its Dative plural, and only two nouns have both: studentowi/studentom and siostrze/siostrom. bratu, mamie, tacie, kobiecie and nauczycielowi have no taught Dative plural (nauczycielom is NEW); dziecku and koledze are NEW, so dzieciom and kolegom have no taught singular. The neuter row on slide 3 therefore carries an EM DASH in the singular column with one line of explanation - the b2_kim_czym / b2_case_gym treatment - rather than a fabricated form.

SLIDE 4 IS THE BLOCK'S SUMMARY BOARD: four oblique cases, three strings (-ych Genitive, -ych Locative, -ymi Instrumental, -ym Dative), with the trigger word that selects each. It is honest about its own scope - these are the four OBLIQUE plural endings, and the Nominative and Accusative plural adjective is not taught anywhere yet, virile or otherwise, so nothing here is claimed to be complete.

PAYS ONE LOGGED INBOX ITEM, exactly as C1-SPINE directed. The reconciliation table's entry "Dative plural noun in the podoba sie frame" reads: "c1_adj_pl_dat's pack, AS A USE ITEM - the ending is owned, only the frame shape is new; logged, not a unit." Use item 7 is that item and only that item: Ten film podoba sie malym dzieciom. a2_dat_chunks taught podoba mi sie with a PRONOUN in the Dative slot; the substitution of a full noun phrase is the frame shape the inbox names, and b1_dative_sg already gave the learner noun Datives after pomagac and dziekowac. One item, not a strand.

FENCED: -ymi appears only in contrast items where z is the trigger, never in a Dative slot; -ych likewise only under duzo / nie ma / w / na / o. -emu and -ej appear only as the SINGULAR Dative forms b2_adj_dat owns, as the singular half of a contrast. -ich is out; every adjective is a hard stem. ciocia is a person noun and takes an adjective only in the Dative plural, never in the Nominative.

PISANIE: eight TWO-word Dative phrases, the c1_adj_pl_gen shape rather than the three-word prepositional shape the Locative and Instrumental units needed. The Dative here is governed by a VERB, not a preposition, so adjective + noun is the whole minimal pattern unit and no governor belongs inside it. Two words, under the cap, pattern phrases and not composed sentences; nothing added to the repair queue. All eight answers distinct under the engine's own norm().

intro.title: -ym, and this time it is a plural
intro.body: The Dative plural asks for -ym on the adjective. You have produced that string twice already and both times it was a singular — once in the Locative, once in the Instrumental. This is the first time it is plural, and there is nothing in the ending itself to say so.

intro.title: The noun settles it, not the adjective
intro.body: The adjective is no help here — it is the same four letters in all three jobs. The noun behind it decides: hotelu and kolegą are singular, and -om is the Dative plural, which nothing else in this course ends in. Read the noun first.

intro.title: Gender stops mattering, for the fourth time
intro.body: The singular Dative made you choose between -emu and -ej. The plural does not. One string covers all three genders, which is now true of every plural case in this block. The neuter singular Dative has not come up in this course, so that row has a plural only.

intro.title: The plural adjective, four cases
intro.body: This is every oblique plural adjective ending the course teaches: three strings across four cases. The adjective never tells you the case on its own — the word in front does, and in the Dative that word is a verb rather than a preposition.

examples.en: I help the new students, but I'm going with good friends.
examples.pl: Pomagam nowym studentom, ale idę z dobrymi kolegami.

match.en: The doctor helps the new patients.
The children help the small cats.

quiz.explain: studentom is a Dative plural, so the adjective takes -ym. nowemu is the singular and would clash with the noun.
Three plural endings now exist and they do not overlap: -ych after dużo, nie ma, w, na and o; -ymi after z; -ym after a verb like pomagać.

quiz.prompt: I help the new student (just one). →
quiz.explain: The singular Dative adjective is -emu. The last option is perfectly good Polish, but it says several students.
This is the very same dobrym as the Dative plural, doing a completely different job — the noun hotelu is singular and w makes it Locative. The ending never tells you the number; the noun does.
ludziom is one of the irregular plurals from B2. The adjective in front of it is completely regular.
pomagać takes the Dative, and -om on the noun makes it plural. nowymi would be right after z, not after this verb.
z is the Instrumental word, so -ymi. Putting -ym after z is the predictable slip now that both endings exist.
w has taken -ych since the Locative unit and still does. Each of the three plural endings belongs to its own set of trigger words.
dziękować takes the Dative just as pomagać does. The last option leaves the noun in the singular Instrumental.

quiz.prompt: The children help the small cats. →
quiz.explain: kotom is the Dative and kotami is the Instrumental — one letter apart and a different case. The verb chooses the Dative, and the adjective follows the noun.

quiz.prompt: I thank the good sister (just one). →
quiz.explain: The feminine singular Dative is -ej. The last option is correct for several sisters — in the plural there is no feminine form to reach for.
dużo has taken the Genitive since A1 and the plural adjective there is -ych. The last option is the plain plural left exactly as it stands.

type_items.explain: dzieciom is neuter and it makes no difference — the plural Dative adjective is the same for every gender.
